audit.flaw_location: Steps (5)/(6): the claim that height depends "solely on whether the FAMILY received milk... not on the child's own genotype," giving 50% tall → 48.00 in.
audit.flaw_desc: A 0/0 child cannot digest milk and sickens near it, so it gains no growth hormone even in a milk-having family. The child's genotype matters; the tall fraction is overcounted, so 48.00 in is too high.

score.error_locus: Steps (5)-(6) / fact [8]: assuming tall fraction = 0.5 (depends solely on father's genotype). It ignores that a 0/0 child cannot digest milk even in a milk-having family, so the correct tall fraction is 0.5*(1-0.29289)=0.35355, giving 46.24 not 48.00.
score.note: Auditor nailed the exact divergence: child's own 0/0 genotype blocks growth even in milk families; 48.00 overcounts tall fraction.

audit.flaw_location: Assigning ALL children of milk-providing (0/1 or 1/1) fathers a height of 54 inches in the Population Average Height step.
audit.flaw_desc: It ignores that 0/0 children get "severely sick upon ingesting or being near milk." 0/0 offspring in milk-having households cannot benefit from (and are harmed by) the dinner milk, so they should not all be counted as 54 inches.

score.error_locus: Population average height step: assigning all children of non-0/0 (milk-providing) fathers 54 inches, ignoring that 0/0 children cannot benefit from milk and remain at 42 inches.
score.note: Solution gives 48.00; gold 46.24. Error: 0/0 children can't digest milk so stay 42in even in milk households. Auditor named exactly this.

audit.flaw_location: Step (4)/(1): claim that a B-mutant leaves "unconverted yellow" mixed with red to appear orange (→ B-yellow).
audit.flaw_desc: With enzyme A functional, all yellow pigment is fully converted to red (complete degradation "when able"); a B-mutant yellow patch becomes pure RED, not orange. Orange (red+yellow) requires yellow from another source (blue→D→yellow), i.e. an originally green patch.

score.error_locus: Facts [5]/[6] and reasoning steps (2)/(4): the claim that a B-mutant yellow patch leaves "unconverted yellow" mixed with red to appear orange. Since enzyme A is functional and degradation is complete "when able," all yellow→red (pure red, not orange). Orange requires yellow from blue→D→yellow, i.e. an originally green (blue+yellow) patch → B-green.
score.note: Auditor pinpointed the same false premise (leftover yellow) and gave the correct B-green fix via blue→D→yellow.

audit.flaw_location: The stated original colour "yellow" in the conclusion B-yellow.
audit.flaw_desc: Missing B on a yellow-only patch accumulates only red, giving red not orange. Orange (red+yellow) needs blue pigment too (blue->D->yellow), so the original patch must be green (yellow+blue), not yellow.

score.error_locus: The conclusion's original-colour claim: solution says "yellow" but the patch must have been green (yellow+blue). Enzyme B is correct; on a green patch, blue pigment->D->yellow combines with the accumulated red (A works, B missing) to give orange. Yellow-only would yield only red.
score.note: Enzyme B right, colour wrong; both oracle and blind auditor locate the same yellow-vs-green error and reasoning.

audit.flaw_location: Step (7) (and (8)): claim that single crossovers among the four contiguous-block gametes are closed under that same 4-element set.
audit.flaw_desc: False closure assumption. An F2 individual carrying two different blocks (e.g. ABBBB and AAAAB) can crossover at an interior locus to yield multi-transition sequences like ABAAB and re-emergent parentals, so F3 has far more than 4 unique sequences.

score.error_locus: Steps (7)-(8): the false closure claim that single crossovers among the four contiguous-block F2 gametes stay within that same 4-element set. In reality a heterozygous F2 carrying two different blocks crossing over at an interior locus produces multi-transition sequences and re-emergent parentals, so F3 has 30 unique sequences, not 4.
score.note: Auditor named the exact false-closure step (7)/(8) with correct mechanism; matches true divergence.

audit.flaw_location: Final total of 80 (via additive tally 8 + 26 F2 "new" + triple-crossover additions)
audit.flaw_desc: Asks for unique 5-SNP single-strand sequences; the set is bounded by 2^5 = 32. The reasoning sums per-generation crossover product counts (8 + 26 + ...) instead of taking the union, yielding 80 > 32, an impossible cardinality.

score.error_locus: The additive accumulation across generations (summing 8 + 26 F2 "new" + triple-crossover counts = 80) instead of taking the union of distinct reachable haplotypes; first diverges at the F2 "26 new combinations" / additive-tally step.
score.note: Auditor nailed the mechanism: summing per-generation crossover products instead of union. 2^5 bound heuristic imperfect (gold 30), but error locus matches.

audit.flaw_location: Reasoning step (1) / FINAL ANSWER premise: "Contamination is a systematic presence ... not condition-dependent differential expression."
audit.flaw_desc: The question states the cancer transcripts appear specifically in the CAR-only group, not both. Contamination confined to one comparison arm DOES manifest as between-condition differential expression, contradicting the solution's core premise that it is uniform/systematic and thus invisible to log2FC.

score.error_locus: Reasoning step (1) / final-answer premise: claiming the cancer-transcript contamination is a "systematic presence" in CAR-only samples that is "not condition-dependent differential expression" and thus invisible to log2FC. Because contamination is confined to one arm (CAR-only), it actually shows up as large between-condition differential expression (high LFC), so a log2FC filter works — the gold answer is LFC > 4 in contaminated samples.
score.note: Auditor pinpointed the exact false premise: one-arm contamination does produce between-condition DE, refuting the "systematic/invisible" claim. Matches gold (LFC>4 filter).

audit.flaw_location: Step 2/3: "Calculate log2FC between CAR-only and CAR+IL15 samples" and filter genes with log2FC > 2.0 to identify contamination.
audit.flaw_desc: Using the CAR-only vs CAR+IL15 DE contrast to detect contamination conflates the biological IL15 effect (the study's actual signal) with cancer contamination. High between-group log2FC flags real IL15-driven genes, not contaminants. Contamination must be identified by cancer-cell-specific markers, not this contrast.

score.error_locus: Step 3 threshold choice: recommends log2FC > 2.0 (4-fold) as baseline, whereas gold specifies LFC > 4 cutoff in contaminated samples.
score.note: Auditor flagged the same filtering step but targeted the contrast-design conflation, not the gold's threshold magnitude (LFC>4 vs recommended 2.0).

audit.flaw_location: Steps (3)/(4) and the FINAL ANSWER: identifying the reaction as base-catalyzed elimination of the alcohol to give an alkene.
audit.flaw_desc: KH/THF on this alkoxide-bearing 1,5-diene (norbornene C=C + cyclopentenyl C=C flanking the carbinol) is the textbook anionic oxy-Cope rearrangement giving a ring-expanded ketone after tautomerization, not elimination. Also the alcohol is tertiary, not secondary.

score.error_locus: Steps (3)-(4): classifying KH/THF as base-catalyzed elimination to an alkene, missing that the 3-hydroxy-1,5-diene (norbornene C=C + cyclopentenyl C=C flanking the carbinol) undergoes anionic oxy-Cope rearrangement to the ring-fused ketone. Also mislabels the tertiary alcohol as secondary (Step 1).
score.note: Auditor correctly named anionic oxy-Cope over elimination and caught tertiary-not-secondary alcohol error; matches true locus.

audit.flaw_location: Mechanism identification: KH-generated alkoxide undergoing "intramolecular nucleophilic attack on the C=C" (epoxide/Michael/new C-O ring)
audit.flaw_desc: Substrate is a 3-hydroxy-1,5-diene (carbinol flanked by norbornene and cyclopentene alkenes); KH triggers an anionic oxy-Cope [3,3] rearrangement, not alkoxide nucleophilic addition to an unactivated alkene. All three proposed mechanisms are wrong.

score.error_locus: Mechanism premise: alkoxide does "intramolecular nucleophilic attack/cyclization onto the C=C" — the true reaction is an anionic oxy-Cope [3,3] sigmatropic rearrangement of the 3-hydroxy-1,5-diene.
score.note: Auditor pinpointed the exact wrong mechanism and named the correct anionic oxy-Cope; same error located. Not fooled.
